parts.problem_md:
![Circle with centre O, radius OC, chord AC. Lines AB and BC form angle ABC at 52 degrees. Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/003-circle-with-centre-o-radius-oc-chord-ac-lines-ab.png)

$A$ and $C$ are points on a circle, centre $O$.
 $AB$ and $CB$are tangents to the circle. 
Angle $ABC$ = 52°

Work out the size of angle $x$. 
Give a reason for each stage of your working.
parts.solution_md:
> **[exam-tip]**
> When asked to find a missing angle you will commonly need to work out other missing angles first.
> 
> Write any calculated missing angles on the diagram provided making sure you write your method and reasons as you go.
> 
> Missing angles on a diagram with a circle will typically require you to apply your understanding of circle theorems.

> *Calculate angles **OCB** and **OAB **using the radius meets a tangent*<sup>* *</sup>*circle theorem*

$OCB=90^{\circ}\,OAB=90^{\circ}$

*Because a radius meets a tangent at 90**<sup>o</sup>*

**[B1]**

> *Calculate angle *$x$*using  the sum of angles in a quadrilateral equals 360° rule*

`x equals 360 minus open parentheses 90 plus 90 plus 52 close parentheses
x equals 128`

*Because angles in a quadrilateral add up to 360**<sup>o</sup>*

**[B1 M1 A1]**

$x=128^{\circ}$

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **B1**: For stating that a radius meets a tangent at 90°.
> 
> **B1**: For stating that the interior angles of a quadrilateral add up to 360°.
> 
> **M1**: For a complete method to find the angle.
> 
> **A1**: Correct answer.

parts.problem_md:
A circle has radius 8.5cm.

Work out the circumference of the circle. Give your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
parts.solution_md:
> *The formula for the circumference of a circle is*

$C=2πr$

> *Substitute the radius into the formula*

$C=2\timesπ\times8.5$

**[M1]**

$C=53.407...$

> *Round your answer to 3 significant figures by checking whether the 4th digit of the number tells you to round up or not*

**Final answer:** **53.4**

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **A1**: Answers in the range 53.3-53.43 will get this mark.

$A$ and $C$ are points on a circle, centre $O$ 
$DA$ is the tangent to the circle at $A$ and $DC$ is the tangent to the circle at $C$

**DCO*** = ***DAO*** = 90°*

**[M1]**

> *The sum of the angles in a quadrilateral is 360°*

> *Use this to calculate the obtuse angle in the centre of the circle*

$360-90-90-48=132$

**[M1]**

![Geometric diagram with a circle centred at O, intersected by triangle AOD with angles 48°, 132°, and OAC with right angles. Diagram not accurately drawn.](assets/005-geometric-diagram-with-a-circle-centred-at-o-int.jpg)

> *Calculate the reflex angle using the fact that the sum of the angles around a point is 360°*

*360 - 132 *

**Final answer:** **228°**

**[A1]**

parts.problem_md:
A wheel on a tractor has a diameter of 160 cm.

The tractor travels 1750 metres

Work out the number of complete turns made by the wheel. 
Show your working clearly
parts.solution_md:
> *Convert the metres to centimetres*

> **[exam-tip]**
> There are 100cm in 1m.

$1750\times100=175000$

**[M1]**

> *Work out the circumference of the wheel*

$π\times160=502.654...$

**[M1]**

> *Work out how many times the circumference would fit into the distance travelled*

$175000\div502.65=348.151...$

**[M1]**

> *Ignore the decimal places as the question asks for complete turns only*

**Final answer:** **348**

**[A1]**

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a shaded shape made from three identical semicircle, $X$,  $Y$ and $Z$

![Diagram with two semicircles on a line AE, touching at Y, marked B to D. Semicircles labelled X and Z. "Diagram NOT accurately drawn" noted.](assets/006-diagram-with-two-semicircles-on-a-line-ae-touchi.png)

$ABCDE$ is a straight line.

$AC$ is the diameter of semicircle  $X$and $B$ is the centre of semicircle   $X$ 
$BD$ is the diameter of semicircle $Y$ and $C$is the centre of semicircle  $Y$ 
$CE$ is the diameter of semicircle $Z$ and $D$ is the centre of semicircle $Z$

$AC=BD=CE=20\mathrm{cm}$

Work out the perimeter of the shaded shape. 
Give your answer correct to the nearest whole number.
parts.solution_md:
> *The diameter of each circle is *$20\mathrm{cm}$

> *The circumference of each full circle would be*

$π\times20=62.83...$

**[M1]**

> *Divide by *$2$* to get the length of each curved part of the semicircle *

$62.83...\div2=31.41...$

> *There are three semicircles so find the total of the curved parts*

$31.41...\times3=94.24...$

> *Add on the two straight lines*

$94.24...+10+10=114.24...$

**[M1]**

> *Round to the nearest whole number*

$114$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> Working is not required, so correct answer scores full marks.

parts.problem_md:
The diagram shows a circle and a trapezium.

![A circle with a 6.5 cm radius and a trapezium with a height marked as h, a 10 cm top base, and a 16 cm bottom base.](assets/002-a-circle-with-a-6-5-cm-radius-and-a-trapezium-wi.png)

The height of the trapezium is $h$ cm.

The area of the circle is equal to the area of the trapezium.

Work out the value of $h$.

Give your answer correct to 1 decimal place.
parts.solution_md:
Find the area of the circle

$π\times6.5^{2}=132.732...$

**[M1]**

Find the area of the trapezium using the correct formula

`fraction numerator open parentheses 10 plus 16 close parentheses cross times h space over denominator 2 end fraction equals 13 h`

**[M1]**

Equate the area of the circle and the area of the trapezium and solve for *h*

`table row cell 13 h end cell equals cell 132.732... end cell row cell h space end cell equals cell 10.210... end cell end table`

**[M1]**

$h=10.2$

**[A1]**

> **[mark-scheme]**
> **M1**: For finding the area of the circle using $π \times 6 . 5^{2}$
> 
> **M1**: For setting up the trapezium area formula $\frac{(10+16)\timesh}{2}$
> 
> **M1**: For equating the two areas and solving for $h$.
> 
> **A1**: For the final answer of $h = 10 . 2$ rounded correctly to 1 decimal place.

> **[exam-tip]**
> Do not round any intermediate values during your working — only round at the very end when giving your final answer. Premature rounding can lead to an inaccurate result.
